newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU annual grain exports well up, but may tail off.
newsitem.headline: EU annual grain exports well up, but may tail off.

text.p: Commercial soft wheat exports from the European Union are about to break the seven-million-tonne mark, one and a half times as much as the amount exported this time last year, official figures showed on Tuesday.
Barley exports have also more than trebled, breaking through four million tonnes, as the EU moves back onto the world market to dispose of last year's bumper crop.
The increase compared with last year is especially steep since the previous campaign was marked by tight supplies and an unusual decision to impose export taxes for wheat and barley.
But France is expected to seize on the chance to raise its key grain export goals when its ONIC grain authority publishes monthly supply estimates on Wednesday, industry sources say.
ONIC is expected to raise its export target for soft wheat in the year to June 30 by 250,000 tonnes to 6.25 million tonnes.
It may also raise its barley export forecast by 400,000 tonnes to 1.5 million tonnes. Both figures cover exports from France to countries outside the 15-nation European Union.
Latest EU export/import figures, supplied by member country officials, show the EU as a whole authorised exports of 6.746 million tonnes of soft wheat between July 1 and February 4.
On top of this the EU granted licences for 211,350 tonnes of soft wheat from the free market on February 6, bringing the totaal for the season just short of seven million tonnes.
Up to February 4 last year the EU had released about 4.5 million tonnes.
Barley approvals up to February 4 this year were 4.058 million tonnes with another 26,000 tonnes granted on February 6.
EU officials say the Commission is willing to cover recent wheat sales to Egypt and other business even if, as happened last week, this means dropping the EU's world price by a few dollars a tonne.
But licences will be allocated on a gradual basis, using the shelter of lower U.S. wheat prices wherever possible to avoid leading the market lower, they said.
Egypt recently bought half a million tonnes of wheat from France in the low $140s per tonne while the last EU wheat award was valued around $145 per tonne on a fob French basis.

Traders said that despite France's export optimism and the Commission's apparent willingness to raise refunds gradually, the chances of exporting 10 million tonnes of wheat this year as many had hoped now appear relatively slim.
"You could see three million tonnes in intervention this year but this is not a dramatic amount," one senior trader said.
Egypt's purchase was seen as one of the last major old-crop wheat deals this season. On the other hand there are quite a few more modest orders around for short-haul grain, traders said.
Total EU export commitments for grain and processed products have reached 19.311 million tonnes, up to February 4, a rise of 41 percent from 13.715 million a year ago, officials said.
Specialist newsletter Agra France reported on Monday that the EU aimed to export 25 million tonnes of grain and products in the full season. The EU has not disclosed a balance sheet.
